english.title: Disclose information that you have assumed a new identity - SOCA 2005

additionalkeywords.additionalkeyword: Serious Organised Crime and Police Act 2005

english.standardoffencewording:
On **(..SPECIFY DATE..) at **(..SPECIFY TOWNSHIP..),

(A)_[being]_
(B)_[having been]_

a protected person who had assumed a new identity in pursuance of arrangements made under section 82(1) of the Serious Organised Crime and Police Act 2005 disclosed information knowing or suspecting that the information disclosed indicated that you had assumed or might have assumed a new identity
english.legislation: Contrary to section 88(1) and (3) of the Serious Organised Crime and Police Act 2005.

english.notes:
(i) Section 89 of the Serious Organised Crime and Police Act 2005 provides defences in relation to the above offence:-
89(1) P is not guilty of an offence under section 88(1) if, at the time when he disclosed the information, it was not likely that its disclosure would endanger the safety of any person.
89(2), (3) and (4) - not applicable to this offence.
89(5) The Secretary of State may by order make provision prescribing circumstances in which a person who discloses information is not guilty in England and Wales or in Northern Ireland of an offence under that subsection.
89(6) - not applicable.
89(7) If sufficient evidence is adduced to raise an issue with respect to a defence under or by virtue of this section, the court or jury must assume that the defence is satisfied unless the prosecution proves beyond reasonable doubt that it is not.

other.penalty:
SUMMARY: Twelve months imprisonment and/or a fine not exceeding the statutory maximum.
INDICTMENT: Two years imprisonment and/or a fine

Until the commencement of section 282 of the Criminal Justice Act 2003 the penalty on summary conviction will be - Six months imprisonment and / or a fine not exceeding the statutory maximum

Time limit for prosecutions:
None

On the 12th March 2015 the limit on fines imposed by a Magistrates’ court was removed – as such, the potential fine on summary conviction in relation to an offence committed after this date is unlimited.
